title: Efficient Sparse Linear Bandits under High Dimensional Data

problem.claim: Sparse linear bandit problems in high-dimensional settings require computationally efficient methods when samples are limited.

gap.claim: Existing feature-selection and dimension-reduction challenges create computational complexity and limit regret performance in high-dimensional sparse linear bandits.

contributions.claim: The Lasso Random Project Bandit (LRP-Bandit) algorithm combines Lasso and Random Projection for feature selection and dimension reduction in sparse linear bandit problems.
The paper derives expected cumulative-regret upper bounds for data-poor and data-rich regimes, including Õ (T2 over 3 s 3 over 2 log7 over 6 d) and Õ (s√T log d), respectively.
The stated regret upper bounds match theoretical minimax lower bounds up to logarithmic factors.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments report that LRP-Bandit is computationally efficient.
Experiments report that LRP-Bandit outperforms other benchmarks on expected cumulative regret.

narrative_sequence.summary: The authors propose LRP-Bandit for sparse linear bandits in high-dimensional, limited-sample settings.
The method combines Lasso-based feature selection with Random Projection for dimension reduction.
The paper gives regret upper bounds for total dimension, significant feature dimension, and sample size.
With samples above a problem-dependent threshold, the regret bound improves in the data-rich regime.
Experiments report computational efficiency and lower expected cumulative regret than benchmark methods.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the problem-dependent threshold for the data-rich regime.
